hook: AI chips could run on less than 1 fJ per operation.

sections.voiceover: AI chips could run on less than 1 fJ per operation.
sections.visual_cue: Close‑up of a futuristic AI chip glowing, overlay showing “<1 fJ” label.

sections.voiceover: On 28 Oct 2026, Brown unveiled ultrathin BiFeO₃ films. Only a few ångströms thick, they sit on 3.94 Å DyScO₃. Will removing the dead‑layer cut AI chip energy below 1 fJ?
sections.visual_cue: Brown University press release image with BiFeO₃ film diagram and a 3.94 Å lattice illustration.

sections.voiceover: But conventional CMOS still consumes 10‑100 fJ per operation today.
sections.visual_cue: Side‑by‑side graphic comparing 10‑100 fJ CMOS energy with the sub‑1 fJ target.

sections.voiceover: Their model shows multiferroic chips consume under 1 fJ, versus 10‑100 fJ for CMOS. That’s an order‑of‑magnitude power cut for AI accelerators. The work, published in Nature Materials by Lucas Caretta and colleagues, marks a turning point.
sections.visual_cue: Animated chart dropping from 10‑100 fJ to <1 fJ, overlay of Nature Materials cover and researcher portraits.

sections.voiceover: AI chips may soon run on sub‑fJ energy, reshaping data‑center power needs.
sections.visual_cue: Final frame of an AI chip powering a data‑center, caption “sub‑fJ era”.
